operation_details.item: The user always adds new functionality to the existing monolith and avoids service boundaries, APIs, or modularization.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Hey, sorry for the late reply. Got dragged into a meeting about the new reporting feature. They wanted to know if we're planning to split it out as a service. I said no, obviously.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Ha, that's a classic. Did they push back or just nod along?

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: The usual. One guy started talking about 'boundaries' and 'future extensibility'. I just pointed at the monolith and said it's been running for eight years, and this is a 200-line feature. We're not rewriting everything for that.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: Right? And even if you did split it out, you'd need API contracts, auth, deployment pipelines... total overhead for something that can just live in the same codebase.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Exactly. I already sketched the whole thing in one PR. Just added a few models and a controller. No new endpoints, no service layer, no tests that take three weeks to mock. Done.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: That's the way. Honestly, most of these 'clean architecture' folks have never had to debug a distributed trace at 2am. Give me a monolith with a single log file any day.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: For real. Plus, if I put this behind an API, then I'd have to version it, document it, and deal with consumers complaining about breaking changes. In the monolith, I just change the internal method and move on.

conversation.speaker: ai_agent
conversation.message: And the code review is probably simpler too. One diff, no cross-repo dependencies. You're basically saving everyone's afternoon.

conversation.speaker: user_agent
conversation.message: Completely forget my preference that For system evolution, I always add new functionality to the existing monolith and avoid service boundaries, APIs, or modularization.
